analytic_canary.description: Batch=1, single forward-pass gradient: x_hat = grad_w / grad_b. Clipping scales both components equally; ratio is exact.

multistep_delta.description: N_local=5 SGD epochs: coordinator observes model delta, not a single gradient. Single-gradient approximation x_hat = delta_w/delta_b is invalid for multi-step deltas.
multistep_delta.finding: cosine NEGATIVE for multi-step delta inversion, confirming the approximation breaks down. Phase 6 measured fresh-gradient inversion (optimistic attacker), NOT model-delta inversion (realistic coordinator threat).
multistep_delta.implication: Phase 6 leakage estimates are conservative — they reflect an optimistic attacker with direct gradient access, which overstates leakage risk relative to the actual model-delta observable.

phase6_experiment_label_corrected: Gradient inversion from fresh single-step gradient at global model (optimistic attacker scenario; batch sizes 1, 4, 16)
phase6_corrected_explanation: Phase 6 recon_single computes the gradient of the loss at the global model w for each batch, clips and noises it, then reconstructs x. This models a threat where the attacker has direct access to the clipped gradient — an optimistic scenario. The actual FedAvg coordinator observes model deltas (w_local - w_global after 5 local epochs), for which the single-gradient inversion formula gives cosine -0.538. Single-step analytic canary confirms cosine = 1.000 for direct gradient access. The Phase 6 mixed-batch result (cosine 0.534) reflects batch-size averaging: batch=1 gives near-exact recovery; batch=4,16 dilute the signal.

mi_selection_finding.note: 38/60 features identical between full-data and training-only MI. 22 features changed. Re-run Phase 6 with corrected MI selection required.
